name: cabuya_adoption
title: Adopt the Cabuya Protocol
summary: From a running application to a measured conformance level: detect the stack, map the data model onto `place`, pass the one human decision, serialize, serve, and loop the validator until it converges. One afternoon of work and exactly one human decision.

placeholders.{stack_guide}: the matched guide under implement/stacks/, from shared/stack-detection.md
placeholders.{feed_path}: where the generated feed lives in the adopter's repository
placeholders.{manifest_url}: the deployed https URL of /.well-known/cabuya.json (or the declared plain path)
placeholders.{target_level}: the level the adopter is aiming at: L1, L2 or L3

tasks.title: Read the repository; write nothing
tasks.goal: Establish the stack, the data model, and the four hosting facts before a single file is written.
acceptance: The stack and framework are identified and confirmed against the fingerprints, not guessed from the UI.
The tables or collections that hold places are named — and so are the ones that hold people.
Four hosting facts are written down: catch-all present or not, robots.txt status, where a root-served static file lives, and the manifest path.
Nothing was written to the repository.
stop_conditions: No detectable data source: say what was looked for and where, and stop. Never scaffold a feed with invented records.

The records are irreducibly personal (a missing-persons registry, case management, an aid-request queue): the ceiling is L1 permanently by rule 7.1 of the specification's exclusions. Quote spec/EXCLUSIONS.md, offer the link-out pattern, and stop.

tasks.title: Build the field crosswalk
tasks.goal: Map the application's fields onto `place`, with every required field accounted for or named as unmapped.
acceptance: The full mapping table is shown to the human before any code is written — the table, not a summary.
`last_confirmed_at` maps to a real confirmation event or to null; never to an edit timestamp.
Every required field is either mapped or named as unmapped with what it would take.
Every unmapped Extended field is omitted, never filled with something plausible.

validation.human: The human has seen the complete mapping table. This is a review, not a command.

stop_conditions: A required field cannot be filled from the application's data and the human does not accept the honest gap: stop and say which field and why.

tasks.title: The PII gate — the one human decision
tasks.goal: Run the deny-list over every candidate column and free-text value, present the findings, and wait for an explicit human yes that names the specific columns.
acceptance: Every candidate column and free-text value was checked against the deny patterns.
The flagged table was presented in the deny-list's format.
The human named the specific columns in their answer; silence, 'sounds good' and partial answers were re-asked by name.
The decision is recorded with decided_by set to human — the ledger schema accepts nothing else.

validation.human: An explicit human decision naming the specific columns. There is no flag that skips this, and no agent may record it on its own authority.

stop_conditions: The human declines or does not answer: the adoption waits here. There is no path around this task.

tasks.title: Generate the feed
tasks.goal: Write the serializer for this stack: envelope first, records second, and only from data the application actually has.
acceptance: No invented data: a missing Extended field is omitted; a missing Core field is reported, never filled.
`last_updated` is set at build or publish time from the data's own maximum — never per request.
Every record carries `public_url`.
The feed route sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` — on that route, not via a widened global middleware.
stop_conditions: Any PII deny-pattern finding over the generated output: halt and ask the human. Never resolve one by editing the deny-list.

tasks.title: Serve the manifest and survive discovery
tasks.goal: Put the manifest where the host actually serves it, and defeat the SPA catch-all before the validator has to find it.
acceptance: The manifest is served at /.well-known/cabuya.json, or at a declared plain path with a link rel=cabuya in the site head where the host refuses dot-directories.
The catch-all exclusion for this stack is in place.
robots.txt returns 200 with text/plain.
The manifest response is JSON — not the SPA shell with a 200.
stop_conditions: The host cannot serve any non-HTML document at a fixed path: say so plainly; L2 is not reachable on this hosting and the honest ceiling is stated.

tasks.title: Loop the validator to convergence
tasks.goal: Run the validator, parse the JSON report, fix, and repeat — to a measured level or an honest stop.
acceptance: The JSON report is parsed, never the human-readable text.
At most 8 iterations; then stop and summarize what remains and why.
A degraded offline run is reported as schema-valid; conformance unmeasured — never as conforming.
The final measured_level is recorded with the report digest.
stop_conditions: Any PII finding: halt the loop and ask a human. Never edit the deny-list to make it pass.
Exit code 3 (transport): the data is not wrong; say so and stop without opening the serializer.
Eight iterations without convergence: something structural — summarize and hand to the human.

tasks.title: Set the conformance target honestly
tasks.goal: Update the manifest's conformance_target and companion fields to what the validator measured — and no higher.
acceptance: conformance_target never exceeds the last measured level, and the measurement is fresh.
license and permitted_use are present and deliberate.
Every manifest write showed the human the diff first.
stop_conditions: The validator cannot run: unmeasured is not a level, and no target is published on the strength of a degraded run.

tasks.title: Open the registry entry
tasks.goal: Prepare the registry pull request so the publisher appears in the network — with consent, not by surprise.
acceptance: The entry matches the manifest: publisher_id, canonical_url, feeds, license.
The human approved opening the pull request before it was opened.
Inclusion is described as listing, never as endorsement.

validation.human: The human approved the pull request. Never open one to any repository without asking.

stop_conditions: The human declines: the feed still conforms and still works; the registry entry can wait.

tasks.title: Consume peer feeds (L3)
tasks.goal: Read other publishers' feeds under the six consumption rules: filter before fetching, honour ttl and crawl policy, dedupe by claim, render with attribution and age.
acceptance: Filtering by status, permitted use and crawl policy happens before the fetch layer exists.
Fetches honour ttl; nothing scrapes.
Rendered peer data carries attribution and age.
The six MUSTs shape the code rather than being retrofitted.
stop_conditions: A peer's crawl policy reserves reuse: that publisher is dropped, even when a human asks directly.

tasks.title: Hand off
tasks.goal: Leave the adopter's repository explaining itself: the diff summary, the measured level in the validator's words, the remaining warnings, and the next step.
acceptance: CABUYA.md, filled in, is in the adopter's repository.
The measured level is reported in the validator's words — or as unmeasured.
Each remaining warning is named with what it would take.
The exact next step is stated.

validation.human: The handoff summary was presented. This closes the working sequence.

tasks.title: Final PII audit
tasks.goal: Run the deny patterns over everything this adoption created — feed, manifest, code, config, the ledger itself — before calling it done.
acceptance: Every file created or changed by the adoption was checked.
Zero person-level values anywhere: no personal names, personal phones, personal emails, personal documents.
Any finding halted the audit and went to the human — none was resolved by weakening a pattern.
stop_conditions: Any finding: halt, present, and wait. A published contact value is cheap to prevent and impossible to undo.

tasks.title: Report what is true
tasks.goal: Summarize the adoption: what shipped, the measured level with its digest, what remains, and the one decision the human made.
acceptance: Every claim in the report traces to the ledger or the validator report.
No conformance language beyond measured_level, and never the word certified.
The remaining warnings and the honest ceiling, if any, are stated.

validation.human: The report was presented to the human. Its claims are checkable against the ledger.
